nodes.title: The gate card a human decides from contains none of the four things a decision needs: 25 of 25 carry a patch path, 0 carry the diff, 0 carry the verifier verdict, 0 carry the task
nodes.body:
w3-attention-gap-card-vs-diff-decision-time asks for a study comparing an evidence-dense card against a raw diff on time-to-decision and false-accept rate. We cannot run that study: one reviewer, who is also the loop's author, and no ground truth on our own diffs beyond the verifier the card is supposed to summarise. What we can measure is its precondition -- **does the card a human actually receives contain the evidence the decision needs?** A format study on a card that holds no evidence measures reading speed on a pointer.

e67 inventories all 25 gate checkpoints in the ledger by field. The payload has two shapes (21 with `node`, 4 without) and both carry the same seven keys: `message`, `prompt`, `node`, `patch`, `attempt`, `score`, `review`. Median size **343 bytes**, max 359. Against the four classes a promotion decision needs:

- **task**: what was asked -- **0 of 25**. The card never says which task this is.
- **diff**: what changed -- **0 of 25**. `patch` is a *path* to the artifact; the word matched, the content did not. 25 of 25 carry the path, 0 carry a diff.
- **verifier**: why the change is believed -- **0 of 25**. No `verifierOk`, no checks block, no exit code, no stdout. The score is present but the score is a number, not a reason.
- **risk**: what this could break -- **0 of 25** as an explicit field; 2 mention holdout anywhere in their text, 0 mention the threshold (`minGain`/`incumbent`).

What the reviewer does get is `review: "git -C <workspace> apply --stat <patch>"`, i.e. a command that prints changed file names and line counts. So the decision procedure the card supports is: read a score, run a command to see *which files*, then open the patch file itself to see *what changed* and judge whether the verifier was measuring the right thing. The card is an index entry, not evidence.

The dwell times are consistent with that reading but do not prove it. 25 of 25 gate checkpoints were answered. Dwell (raised at -> answered at): min 46 s, p25 130 s, **median 261 s**, p75 1,916 s, max 245,439,279 ms (a checkpoint left open for 2.8 days). Split by decision: **reject median 417 s (n=22) vs approve median 76 s (n=3)**. Rejections took 5.5x longer. Two explanations fit and this data cannot separate them: (a) rejecting requires establishing that something is wrong, which needs the patch; approving needs only a score above the bar, which the card supplies; (b) rejections cluster on the anomaly/stale-baseline checkpoints that were opened and then abandoned while I worked on something else, so the dwell is queue time, not reading time. (a) is the more useful hypothesis and it is testable -- apply the same split to checkpoints whose payload does carry a verdict -- but n=3 approvals means neither estimate is a rate.

The actionable part does not depend on resolving that: **the card cannot be made more evidence-dense by measuring format, because it holds no evidence of any class.** If the format question is worth a study, the first change is to put the verifier's verdict, the task id, and the earned-reason into the payload, then re-measure dwell -- and the ledger already records everything needed to fill those fields at the moment the checkpoint is raised.
nodes.source: research/exp/e67.mjs over ~/.dsh/loom/campaigns/*/events.jsonl; payload built at src/runtime/round.js:2099-2107

nodes.title: A measurement's precondition can be checked even when the measurement cannot be run, and checking it is usually the cheaper and more decisive move
nodes.body:
The question asked for a controlled study of two presentation formats with time-to-decision and error rate as outcomes. Every part of that is out of reach here: two formats need a between-subject design or a counterbalanced one, error rate needs a ground-truth verdict for each candidate diff, and the only reviewer available wrote the loop being reviewed. The temptation is to write 'we cannot measure this' and move on -- which is what the question had been doing for three research waves.

What broke the loop was asking what the study assumes. It assumes both formats carry the evidence. e67 checked that assumption against the 25 cards actually raised and found the card carries a patch path and a number: 0 of 25 contain the diff, the verifier verdict, or the task. So the study as specified would compare a diff against a pointer-to-a-diff, and its result would be about whether people bother to follow a pointer, which we already know from the dwell asymmetry (reject 417 s vs approve 76 s).

This is the general shape and it recurs: `exp-oracle-002` measured that 93 of 105 tasks expose an oracle file before proposing to protect it; `exp-gap-008` measured that the sort key was a constant before rewriting the sort; `exp-brief-001` measured that 69% of the brief is a fixed template before proposing to shrink it; `e55` measured that 0 of 461 patches were whitespace-only before writing a rule against whitespace. In each case the cheap check either made the expensive work unnecessary or pointed at the real defect. The rule worth keeping: **when a study is blocked, enumerate its preconditions and measure those -- a precondition that fails is a stronger result than the study would have been, because it explains why nobody has run it.**

The limit: a precondition check only addresses the direction it checked. Our cards lacking the verifier verdict does not mean evidence-dense cards would help if built -- w8-attention found absolute confidence is useless and relative confidence is not, and the Sidecar study found added density doubled mental demand. So the honest status of the format question after this is: the current card is not a test of it, and building an evidence-carrying card is a prerequisite for having an opinion.
nodes.source: research/exp/e67.mjs; contrast with exp-oracle-002, exp-gap-008, exp-brief-001, research/exp/e55.mjs

gaps.title: Would a card carrying the verifier verdict and the task id change human dwell time or false-accept rate, and can one reviewer with no ground truth answer that at all?
gaps.body: e67 established the current card carries neither the verdict nor the task, so the format comparison has never been run against an evidence-carrying card. The natural next step is to add `verifierOk`, `earnedReason`, `taskId` and the holdout result to the gate payload and re-measure dwell. Two problems. First, the reviewer is the loop's author, so 'would you have caught this' is not an independent measurement -- and w8-attention already found reviewers cannot report whether they checked (79% of missed silent defects were rated 4-5/5 confidence). Second, false-accept needs a ground truth verdict for each candidate, and the only candidate verdict we have is the verifier, which is the thing being summarised; the holdout is the one independent check and it fires on 3 of 61 rounds (exp-gap-010), far too rarely to power a rate. So the honest version of this question is narrower: with the verdict in the card, does dwell time fall, and does the reviewer's stated reason for rejecting ever cite evidence that was in the card? The second is checkable from the answer notes already being recorded and does not need ground truth.
